summary: Use QGIS to assess water-service coverage, monitoring sites, and spatial priorities. Explore the five-day course outline and enrol.
lede: Spatial data analysis for water management helps GIS analysts and water planners turn mapped service, asset and monitoring data into planning evidence. Using QGIS and GeoPackage workflows, participants check coordinate systems and data quality, assess service and monitoring coverage, analyse access, and prioritise fieldwork locations. They also create reviewable maps and communicate assumptions, limitations and data lineage; advanced hydrological modelling is covered at overview level.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who use mapped water, service, infrastructure, or environmental data to plan work and explain spatial priorities.
prerequisites: Intermediate GIS experience is expected, including basic layer handling and map navigation. No programming is required. Bring a laptop with QGIS installed; the course uses QGIS and supplied practice datasets, with no personal account required.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
